E08 VERIFY, all driver-run: build EXIT=0 at 1710 static pages (was 762), compiled in 3.0s; the narrowed safety gate reports '3 sentinels, 11 allowed hit(s) under /cerebro/signal/, 0 leaks across 5273 files - feed OK index OK daily OK archive OK weekly OK'. SABOTAGE PROOF: injecting a REAL sentinel into a feed description produced '[safety] FAIL: 30 scraped-body occurrence(s) outside the per-signal route' and BUILD_EXIT=1, so the gate can still fail. The driver's FIRST sabotage attempt was itself broken - the sentinel extraction returned '{' - and was caught and redone rather than being recorded as a pass. index.json stayed body-free: 407787 raw / 104895 gzip for 945 records, fields unchanged, growth proportional to the corpus only. Backlinks render '38 briefings' with 38 distinct daily links for SnapState, matching the driver's independently computed fan-in exactly. Graph: 84 nodes, 119 edges, tag and domain labels, click navigates, no horizontal overflow at 390px, renders on mobile; the page itself opens by explaining that 0 of 945 notes carry an outgoing link and that a note-link graph would be 63 hubs and 945 leaves telling the reader nothing - it documents the measurement instead of pretending. Signal pages carry explicit attribution: 'automated extraction of the article at <url>, stored verbatim in the public cerebro-vault repository. Copyright remains with the original publisher.' TWO OBSERVATIONS FOR STEVIE, neither blocking: (1) the SnapState note's scraped body is a Cloudflare Access LOGIN PAGE, not an article, so publishing bodies will sometimes publish extraction junk; (2) signal pages are self-canonical while republishing third-party text - a cross-domain canonical to the original is the standard mitigation, but it would effectively de-index them, which contradicts his explicit choice to index.
